response.rationale: Both answers correctly denote a classroom whiteboard. Indonesian usage supports “papan tulis putih,” while Malaysian terminology explicitly supports “papan putih.” The different-common-word relation is defensible as a national preference, though both languages may also use the English borrowing “whiteboard.” No false-friend contrast is present.
